If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.00 on day 1–2, reduce forecast peak by 3–5% in late horizon (days 20–30) to counteract momentum overcorrection.  
If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, suppress forecast rise by 2–4% in early horizon (days 1–5) to prevent false bullish signals.  
When sentiment shifts from negative to positive over 2 consecutive days, increase forecast slope by 1–3% in mid-horizon to capture sentiment-driven reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and true price shows strong upward momentum, add 1–2% upward bias in late horizon to align with sentiment lag.  
If model forecast consistently underestimates true price by >3% over 3 consecutive days, apply +2% correction to next forecast if sentiment remains positive.
